scope: Tiny paired local contracts;root-owned runtime qualification is separate.

cases.title: Implement the pure scalar rule precisely
cases.input_contract: ReturnNULL/None unchanged;collapse only space, tab, newline andcarriage return runs, trim ordinary spaces, and translateASCII A-Z to a-z. Preserve otherUnicode code points.
cases.expected: All 12 golden outputs, includingcafÉ,İi, nonbreaking-space-wrapped a and unchanged decomposed e-plus-accent.
cases.verification: Apply the scalar function to every raw fixture value and compare with all golden pairs.

cases.title: Express the same rule with native Spark functions
cases.input_contract: Produce id, normalized using translate, regexp_replace andtrim on the label column. PreserveNULL propagation and the exact golden values.
cases.expected: The twelve ordered output pairs equal the golden fixture and normalized has string type.
cases.verification: Assert the full pair list andStringType;do not accept agreement with only one UDF implementation.

cases.title: Wrap the scalar rule with a declared UDF return type
cases.input_contract: Create a ScalaString UDF or a PythonStringType scalar UDF with useArrow=False, then return id, normalized. Keep the function pure and validate all outputs.
cases.expected: Every pair matches the same twelve golden values. Python uses the non-Arrow scalar path;Scala stays in the JVM.
cases.verification: Assert all golden pairs and string result type for the enabled language-specific UDF.

cases.title: Locate the execution boundary in physical evidence
cases.input_contract: Return the physical plan strings for the built-in and language-specific UDF relations. Identify Python evaluation only where it is actually present.
cases.expected: Python UDF plan containsBatchEvalPython;built-in contains noPython evaluator. Scala UDF expression is present withoutBatchEvalPython orArrowEvalPython.
cases.verification: Assert the language-appropriate markers and print both plans;do not infer a speed ratio from them.

cases.title: Preserve missing, empty and ordinary-text populations
cases.input_contract: Classify normalized values as missing, empty or text and count each category. Separately select the identity whose normalized text equals the literal null.
cases.expected: Missing 1, empty 2, text 9. Literal null text belongs only toID 12;unknown value belongs only toID 1.
cases.verification: Assert all category counts and both exact identity selections for built-in and UDF results.

cases.title: Reject a plausible but semantically broader implementation
cases.input_contract: Validate a result against the full golden sequence. Deliberately apply general lowercasing and default trimming without interior-whitespace collapse, and require rejection.
cases.expected: The wrong implementation disagrees at least onIDs 4,5,6,9. Python additionally removes the preserved nonbreaking spaces atID 8.
cases.verification: Assert named mismatch identities and that the golden validator raises rather than accepting a visually plausible normalization.

golden.optional_dependencies: Arrow/pandas path disabled until a dedicated profile records exact package pins and runtime qualification.
